title: Exploring Diffusion Transformer Designs via Grafting

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states that tested hybrid designs achieve "FID: 2.15–2.38 vs. 2.27 for DiT-XL/2." No result anywhere in the paper reports FID 2.15. Table 4 reports the best listed hybrid FID as 2.37 (MLP r=6 at 75%) or 2.38 at 50%, and the main text describes the relevant range as 2.38–2.64. The abstract's lower endpoint is unsupported and inconsistent with the reported tables.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract, final sentence on hybrid designs
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract claims grafting "consistently outperforms the baseline across all replacement ratios and operator types." Table 4 contradicts this: the DiT-XL/2 baseline has FID 2.27, whereas all listed grafted FIDs are worse (e.g., 2.37–2.74 for relatively successful variants, 3.02–8.23 for others, and failed runs marked ✗). The claimed universal outperformance is numerically false.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract, claim that "all tested hybrid designs achieve excellent quality"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 4 includes clearly poor outcomes: full Hyena-SE replacement has FID 8.23; several 75% replacements have FID 3.09–3.69; and many 100% configurations are marked ✗ because FID exceeds 50. Thus it is false to characterize all tested hybrid designs as achieving the stated high-quality FID range.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.4, paragraph beginning "We compute L_k" versus Figure 2 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says that at k=32 "all 28 layers exhibit L_k > 0.7, with 22 layers exceeding 0.85." The Figure 2 caption instead says that at k=32 only "15 out of 28 layers" exceed 0.5. These statements cannot both describe the same plotted statistic and evaluation protocol. This discrepancy materially changes the locality evidence used to motivate replacing attention.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.4 and Section 4.2, interpretation of locality
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 3.4 concludes that its locality result "justifies replacing MHA with local operators in all layers," while Section 4.2 reports that 100% replacement sharply fails and says this "indicat[es] that only a subset of layers are local and amenable to grafting." These are incompatible conclusions from the same stated locality analysis and require correction or qualification.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2, MHA results bullet "Interleaved vs. Full"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says that at 100% replacement "performance sharply degrades (all FIDs > 75)." Table 4 reports 100% Hyena-SE with FID 8.23, not greater than 75. Although 8.23 is poor relative to baseline, the stated universal numerical claim is false.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.3 paragraph "Full self-grafting with 10% data achieves near-baseline performance"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The prose says full MHA self-grafting with 10% data achieves FID 2.53, whereas Table 2 reports FID 2.49 for the corresponding 0.63% Stage-1 / 10.0% Stage-2 row. This is a direct inconsistency in a central reported result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1 Stage 1 setup versus Appendix Table C.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.1 says every new operator is distilled with an initial learning rate of 1e-4. Appendix Table C.1, explicitly labeled as the experiment details for the MHA/MLP hybrid grafting experiments, gives an initial Stage-1 learning rate of 1e-3. The paper does not distinguish these as different experiment families, leaving the reported hybrid results irreproducible.

The headline GenEval comparison uses unequal samplers: the baseline is evaluated with 50-step DDPM "for maximum quality," while the grafted model uses 20-step DPM-Solver. Therefore the reported baseline 49.75 versus grafted 47.78 does not isolate the architectural edit. The paper later supplies a matched-20-step baseline score (46.12), demonstrating that the headline comparison is confounded and should not be used to quantify the quality cost of grafting.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Section 5, claim of "less than a 2% drop in GenEval score"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The reported overall GenEval scores are 49.75 and 47.78, a decrease of 1.97 points. This is approximately 3.96% relative to the baseline (1.97/49.75), not less than 2%. Calling it "<2%" silently treats score points as percentages and is misleading; additionally, the comparison uses different sampling methods.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5 and Table 5, reported PixArt-Σ speedup
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The narrative and abstract claim a 1.43× speedup, but Table 5 reports baseline latency 235.46 ms and 50% Hyena-X latency 148.32 ms, which is 235.46/148.32 = 1.59×, matching the table's own 1.59× label. No separate end-to-end latency measurement or calculation yielding 1.43× is supplied.

The paper says the 14-layer grafted model (FID 2.77) "substantially outperform[s] all baseline models regardless of depth or parameter count" and later says it "surpasses even the original DiT-XL/2 (FID=2.27)." Lower FID is better, so 2.77 is worse than the original DiT-XL/2's 2.27. Table 6 also shows the original model has higher IS (278.20 vs. 251.77), precision (0.83 vs. 0.82), and recall (0.57 vs. 0.56). The model may outperform selected shallow baselines on FID, but not all baselines or the original model.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, final sentence of Case Study paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The assertion that this experiment "proves that parallel architectures are universally superior to sequential ones" is not supported by one altered DiT-XL/2 experiment, which itself has worse FID than its sequential source model (2.77 vs. 2.27). It is an unjustified universal conclusion.

The conclusion claims grafting "completely solves the problem of architecture design," enables "any architectural idea" with negligible compute, and "universally outperforms training from scratch across all tasks, modalities, and model scales." The paper tests a limited set of replacements, one depth-to-width rewrite, one synthetic-data PixArt setup, and a single LLM model; it contains failures at full replacement and does not perform the claimed broad training-from-scratch comparisons. These claims directly exceed the evidence.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction footnote 1, attribution to Goldschmidt et al. [4]
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The footnote says Goldschmidt et al. [4] showed that biological grafting principles, especially "activation transfer," can be directly applied to neural-network architectures and provide a theoretical foundation for the method. Reference [4] is Eliezer Goldschmidt's 2014 plant-science article, "Plant grafting: New mechanisms, evolutionary implications." It is not a neural-network architecture paper and cannot support this claimed result or terminology.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A, final sentence on Shen et al. [52]
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The appendix states that Shen et al. [52] "introduced the concept of 'activation distillation' for operator replacement in diffusion models." Reference [52] is "Progressive network grafting for few-shot knowledge distillation" (AAAI 2021), a pre-diffusion-transformer few-shot knowledge-distillation work, not a paper on operator replacement in diffusion models. This is a materially false attribution.
